gist: anonymous slow players, host leaves, no dead hand call
title: Fun but……
text: Mahjong is a fun and addictive game, and this app captures the enjoyment of playing. I like that it’s free, which is definitely its biggest advantage.  That said, the app doesn’t seem to be designed with the player experience in mind. There are several areas that could be improved. Because players are anonymous, some people play extremely slowly, or the host may leave in the middle of a game without any consideration for the other players, which can end the game for everyone. There is also no option to call a hand dead, which can make games unnecessarily frustrating. Another area I would love to see improved is audio management. If you are the last one to join a game, you often don’t have time to decide whether all players have audio enabled. It would be much better to set this in the settings so the player’s preference applies to every game, instead of having to change it each time.  I would love to see the developers address these issues and add features that improve the overall playing experience. With a few thoughtful updates, this could easily become an outstanding app. Until then, it’s still worth trying because it’s free and the game itself is always enjoyable.

Also, the cards I’ve seen in person tend to show when some set of tiles is interchangeable (eg if you can use red dragons or green dragons or if you can use lower or higher numbers). The suggested hands feature does adapt to what you have but does not show you when there’s another option, or if it does I haven’t found it.   Finally, the reason for the one-star reduction is because of sound. This app makes the volume of anything I’m listening to on my phone drop down significantly and then when I leave the app, the volume blares because I had to turn it up to hear anything. title: Pretty good, but needs improvement
text: (Updated review) From my original review, "When you declare a Mah Jong, you can't really review the other players' hands, you only see what they racked. Also, the purported hands you can go for are not limited by the tiles already discarded. The latter is a nit, as you can see for yourself which tiles were discarded but it is still misleading. "  The developer's response to the former of these last two points were that in real life you wouldn't be able to see the player's tiles and see their strategy.  Well, this isn't real life, and the name of this app contains "Practice" which implies to me that you should be able to analyze what real players *might* be thinking, as we do in practice games when players are brand new.  If you are truly trying to teach someone you are not worried about "exposing your strategy".    If the game didn't want to give this level of help, then it should also not tell players what hands are available to them or give them any help at all.  Let them think for themselves!  Actually, this would be a great option in any case-- a no-help option that requires them to have their own card and figure things out for themselves as in a real game.  In my initial review I was totally wrong about picking up a pair with a joker-- I am a beginner and was thinking of picking up a pair for Mah Jong with the tile in the pair itself.  My rating remains the same.

title: A great way to practice!
text: I am new to Mahjong and have found this app to be a very beneficial way to learn the hands and start to see patterns faster. I really like being able to see the potential hands in "real" time and also being able to turn that feature off when I am ready to challenge myself. The controls are hyper sensitive, though, so if I happen to have a finger resting on my iPad in just the wrong spot, tiles will be discarded without me even noticing sometimes. Must. Keep. Fingers. Away. The only real issue I wish would be corrected is that the Concealed Hands in the Tiles list should be hidden once a partial hand is exposed. I have Mahjonged numerous times only to realize later that, as in the real game, it should not have counted. As a newbie, I often miss this and feel I would learn better if this responded appropriately. Additionally, one interface feature that would be helpful is the ability to switch where the discard pile is. It would be more comfortable for many of us to play left-handed, but as it is playing that way means the left arm has to reach over and it covers the board. An otherwise terrific app--thank you! **Edit: To be clear, if I try to Mahj on a hand that is not on the card, the app shows me that it is not allowed. Similarly, it would be helpful if the app would disallow a Concealed hand with an already partial exposure.

title: Great practice but very frustrating when playing with computers
text: This app came highly recommended by our Mah Jongg teacher. I am playing it a lot and it has helped me with my game and also to become more familiar with the new game card.  The reason I have deducted two stars is that there are many aspects which frustrate me when I play against the computers.  1) the randomiser isn’t very random. I more often than not pick up the same tile at least three times in a row. Also, the computers win with the same hands over and over again. 2) the amount of times the computers win within the first 10-15 hands is incredible. And many times they do so with concealed hands. It just doesn’t seem realistic and is very frustrating.  3) the computers seem to get a lot of jokers or the right tiles to exchange the jokers, often two at the same time. I know it can happen but it seems to be happening more than it realistically would 4) the computers are not given human reaction speeds. They often call a tile before it is even fully announced and the tiles land on their rack within that time as well.  5) this might be my lack of understanding as I’m pretty new to the game, but when a computer Mah Jonggs it happens so fast that I often don’t understand what happened. No tile is called and they Mah Jongg. I can usually work out what happened after the fact but it often isn’t obvious at first.  6) the app often is delayed and then plays catchup by going extra fast for a couple of tile pickups. I’m wondering if that occurs mostly when the number of players online has increased and the system is overloaded?  In conclusion, I do think I’m getting a lot of practice with this app, and I have learned more detailed rules whilst playing. I also know the game card very well, as I have been given many opportunities to try every section of the card.  I am just very frustrated by the points above and often abandon the game after too much frustration has taken me over. So, I think it is fair to say that I have very mixed emotions about this app. I do feel that the monthly cost is high considering the many flaws of the app. I would appreciate an annual cost that is much reduced, like many apps offer.

title: Fine when playing with others
text: I enjoy using this app to play with friends. When play8 g with the computer, though, it is unrealistic and doesn’t follow the logic most maj players would follow. Example: with two tiles played, Computer #2 calls for a 1 and reveals a quint hand using two 1’s and three jokers. Computer #3 and Computer #1 proceed to cannibalize two of the jokers, all within the first five tiles played. Most maj players would never reveal a quint hand with three jokers extremely early in the game, knowing that 1) they are basically giving away two jokers,  2) there is an excellent chance of getting at least one other of the 1s when it is discarded, and 3) Using three jokers so early in the game would make it very tough to maj with a quint hand. I also find that the computer seems to constantly win with the same hands- quints, concealed hands, NEWS, and 2020 - hands that are not played every game. The computer is always playing the concealed hand under consecutive run. Seriously? Its nice to have the “solitaire” feature with this app, but just be prepared to be very frustrated.

gist: pace selection, friend chat, past cards

gist: no help section, cannot lay out sets or swap jokers

title: Thank you!

gist: keep playing after lockdown, learn new card

gist: solo or friends, wants more jokers

text: This is a wonderful app that lets me play alone, against three computers, or even better against my friends. Of course, if I could just get a few more jokers it would be even better!

gist: improved seeing hands, pricey but valuable

I have never written a review for an app before, but this one deserves it.  It’s pricey but the value is there.

gist: great iOS app, subscription worth it

If you’re an avid player-no matter what level-subscription is well worth the price! THANK YOU!

title: I AM THRILLED TO HAVE IT AT MY FINGERTIPS

title: Great for all levels of play

If you do the free trial, you’ll be subscribing when it’s done!

title: Enhance your game
